items.basis: The cyclone-to-vane-to-coalescer separation train lacks validation of droplet capture efficiency at each stage, with no evidence that the staged approach achieves the claimed 7°C dew point reduction across three stages at 8 bar pressure
The candidate fails to address how the separator performs under variable flow conditions beyond the specified 5 m3/h, making it unsuitable for real-world applications with demand cycling
The candidate provides no empirical data to support the claimed dew point reduction or pressure drop measurements, making the entire prediction speculative

Without comparative testing against existing separators, there's no evidence this design outperforms the status quo, especially since the claimed 2°C dew point is still above typical instrument requirements
The 0.8-1.6mm vane gap in stage 2 is impractical for manufacturing at scale and would likely clog immediately in real compressed air systems containing oil aerosols
The ±1°C tolerance on dew point measurements is too wide to validate the claimed performance, and the candidate doesn't specify how temperature, pressure, and humidity are measured at each stage
